_comment: Expected repository ruleset policy. .github/workflows/security.yml compares
this against the rules actually applied to the default branch and reports
drift. Deleting this file opts this repository out of the check entirely,
which is what forks and upstream copies should do.
Why alerts_threshold and not security_alerts_threshold: zizmor alerts carry
security_severity_level = null, so security_alerts_threshold can never match
any zizmor finding. alerts_threshold: errors is the field that actually
blocks. This was verified by driving a pull request to BLOCKED and back to
CLEAN. Do not 'correct' this back to the documented field; it does nothing.
Known limit, stated so nobody over-trusts the check: the branch rules API
does not report `enforcement`, and that field needs Administration: read,
which GITHUB_TOKEN does not have. This verifies that the policy is present,
not that it is actively enforcing. A ruleset left in evaluate (dry run) mode
is not detected here and would provide no protection.
CI deliberately does not create or repair this ruleset. A workflow that
maintains its own guardrails can be edited to weaken them, and it would
require an admin-scoped credential in CI. See issue #10 for the reasoning.
Recreate with the API if it is ever lost:
POST /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rulesets
target branch, conditions.ref_name.include ["~DEFAULT_BRANCH"],
rules [{ type: code_scanning, parameters: { code_scanning_tools:
[{ tool: zizmor, alerts_threshold: errors, security_alerts_threshold: none }] } }]
